name: Celer cBridge
rootCause: Celer said that cBridge's front-end interface suffered from DNS cache poisoning attacks. This attack targeted third-party DNS providers. Celer's own contract was not affected, and users who suffered losses in this incident, Celer, will be fully compensated.

descriptions.text: Celer said that cBridge's front-end interface suffered from DNS cache poisoning attacks. This attack targeted third-party DNS providers. Celer's own contract was not affected, and users who suffered losses in this incident, Celer, will be fully compensated.

Celer cBridge's frontend was compromised on August 17, 2022, through a BGP/DNS hijack, enabling the attacker to redirect users to malicious contracts and steal approximately $240,000. Protocol and core contracts remained unaffected. A BGP/DNS hijack at the infrastructure level allowed the attacker to alter frontend routing, serving a tampered UI that directed users to attacker-controlled contracts. There was no smart contract vulnerability.
